question:
Select the option that is related to the fourth letter cluster in the same way as the first letter cluster is related to the second letter cluster and fifth letter cluster is related to sixth letter cluster.

TL : GO :: ? : DJ :: SJ : HQ
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. WQ.

GIVEN

• TL : GO :: ? : DJ :: SJ : HQ

SOLUTION

• The rule is the opposite-letter transform (A↔Z, B↔Y … i.e. position → 27 − position).

• TL → G(27−20=7)O(27−12=15) = GO ✓; SJ → H(27−19=8)Q(27−10=17) = HQ ✓.

• So ? is the opposite of DJ: D(4)→27−4=23=W, J(10)→27−10=17=Q → ? = WQ.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Each pair is just opposite letters. Take the opposite of DJ = WQ directly.

NOTE

• Opposite letter = 27 − position (EJOTY/opposite-pair table): A-Z, B-Y, C-X, D-W, J-Q, T-G, L-O, S-H.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

? , AG, XB, UW, RR, OM, LH, IC
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. DL.

GIVEN

• ? , AG, XB, UW, RR, OM, LH, IC

SOLUTION

• First letters: A(1), X(24), U(21), R(18), O(15), L(12), I(9) → decreasing by 3, so the term before A is 1+3 = 4 = D.

• Second letters: G(7), B(2), W(23), R(18), M(13), H(8), C(3) → decreasing by 5, so the term before G is 7+5 = 12 = L.

• Missing first term = DL.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• First letter −3 chain, second letter −5 chain. Step one back: A+3=D, G+5=L → DL.

NOTE

• For letter series, split each cluster and treat every position as its own arithmetic progression (A=1 … Z=26).

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

MY, KX, IV, GS, ?, CJ, AD, YW
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. EO.

GIVEN

• MY, KX, IV, GS, ?, CJ, AD, YW

SOLUTION

• First letters: M(13), K(11), I(9), G(7), ?, C(3), A(1) → −2 each, so ? = 7−2 = 5 = E.

• Second letters: Y(25), X(24), V(22), S(19), ?, J(10), D(4) → differences −1, −2, −3, −4, −5, −6; after S(19) subtract 4 → 15 = O.

• Missing term = EO.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• First letter drops by 2 (G→E). Second letter gap grows 1,2,3,4… so S−4 = O → EO.

NOTE

• When differences themselves change (−1, −2, −3…), it is a second-level series — track the gap pattern separately.

question:
In the following question, set of letter clusters are given. The letter clusters of each set are related to the letter clusters of the same set by some Logic/Rule/Relation. From the given alternatives, select a group of letter clusters which follows the same Logic/Rule/Relation.

(HL, CG, XT)

(IU, DP, WK)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (KU, FP, UK).

GIVEN

• Model sets: (HL, CG, XT) and (IU, DP, WK)

SOLUTION

• In each set every cluster has the SAME internal gap: HL/CG/XT have gap 4 (H+4=L, C+4=G, X−4=T); IU/DP/WK have gap 12 (I+12=U, D+12=P, W−12=K).

• Test the options for one constant internal gap:

• (KU, FP, UK): K+10=U, F+10=P, U−10=K → constant gap 10 ✓ (others have unequal gaps).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Just check the letter-gap inside each of the three clusters; pick the option where all three gaps are equal.

NOTE

• The third cluster usually wraps the alphabet, so the gap shows as negative but its magnitude stays the same.

question: If the month of March 2025 started on Friday, then which date was the first Monday of August 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 5.

GIVEN

• 1 March 2025 = Friday.

SOLUTION

• Days from 1 Mar to 1 Aug = Mar 31 + Apr 30 + May 31 + Jun 30 + Jul 31 = 153 days.

• 153 ÷ 7 gives remainder 6, so 1 Aug = Friday + 6 = Thursday.

• Aug 1 Thu, 2 Fri, 3 Sat, 4 Sun, 5 Mon → first Monday = 5.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Count only odd days: Mar–Jul give 153 mod 7 = 6. Fri + 6 = Thu on 1 Aug; next Monday is the 5th.

NOTE

• Month odd-days: Mar 3, Apr 2, May 3, Jun 2, Jul 3 → 13 → 6 odd days. Add to the start day to jump months.

question: If the month of June 2017 ended on Monday, then which date was the first Tuesday of November 2017?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 4.

GIVEN

• 30 June 2017 = Monday, so 1 July 2017 = Tuesday.

SOLUTION

• Days from 1 Jul to 1 Nov = Jul 31 + Aug 31 + Sep 30 + Oct 31 = 123 days.

• 123 ÷ 7 gives remainder 4, so 1 Nov = Tuesday + 4 = Saturday.

• Nov 1 Sat, 2 Sun, 3 Mon, 4 Tue → first Tuesday = 4.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• 1 Jul = Tue. Jul–Oct = 123 mod 7 = 4 odd days → 1 Nov = Sat; first Tuesday is the 4th.

NOTE

• 'Month ended on Monday' means the last date is Monday, so the 1st of the next month is the following day (Tuesday).

question: The calendar for the year 2021 will be the same as which of the following years?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 2027.

GIVEN

• Base year 2021 (an ordinary/non-leap year).

SOLUTION

• Add odd days year by year (ordinary = 1, leap = 2) until the total is a multiple of 7:

• 2021(1)+2022(1)+2023(1)+2024(2)+2025(1)+2026(1) = 7 odd days.

• 7 is divisible by 7, so the calendar repeats in 2027.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• For an ordinary year that is 1 year after a leap year, its calendar repeats after 6 years → 2021 + 6 = 2027.

NOTE

• A calendar repeats only when cumulative odd days = 0 (mod 7) AND both years are of the same type (leap/ordinary).

question: 5 persons J, K, L, M and N are sitting in a row facing north (not necessarily in the same order). N and M are at the extreme ends of the row. K is the immediate neighbour of J and M. L is to the left of J. How many persons are sitting to the right of L?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 3.

GIVEN

• 5 persons facing north; N and M at extreme ends; K is the immediate neighbour of both J and M; L is to the left of J.

SOLUTION

• K neighbours M and J, so the block is M–K–J with M at an end.

• Take positions left→right (west→east): N _ _ _ M. Place M–K–J at the right end: … J K M.

• Final order: N, L, J, K, M (L sits left of J, satisfying the clue).

• To the right of L are J, K, M = 3 persons.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Fix the M–K–J block against M's end, drop N on the other end; the only gap left of J takes L → 3 people sit to its right.

NOTE

• Facing north: the person's left = west, right = east, so 'right' means the higher positions in a west-to-east row.

question: Price of 6 bags B, C, D, E, F and G is compared. Price of no two bags is same. Number of bags having price less than B are 'X – 2'. Number of bags having price more than D are 'X'. Price of E is third lowest. Price of C is less than F but more than G. Price of D is not lowest. Price of which bag is more than G but less than D?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. E.

GIVEN

• 6 bags, all different prices; bags cheaper than B = X−2; bags costlier than D = X; E is 3rd lowest; G < C < F; D is not lowest.

SOLUTION

• Rank low→high (1 = cheapest … 6 = costliest). E is 3rd lowest → E at rank 3.

• B's rank = (X−2)+1 = X−1; D's rank = 6−X. Taking X = 2: B = rank 1, D = rank 4 (D not lowest ✓).

• Remaining ranks 2,5,6 fit G < C < F → G=2, C=5, F=6.

• Order: B(1) < G(2) < E(3) < D(4) < C(5) < F(6).

• Bag more than G but less than D = rank 3 = E.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Only X = 2 keeps B and D off the 3rd slot (E) and off the lowest; that instantly fixes B lowest, D=4th, and E between G and D.

NOTE

• In ranking puzzles convert every 'number of items above/below' clue into an exact rank, then slot the strict inequalities.

question: Two figures given on the left side of (::) are related with some logic/rule/relation. Select the missing figure on the right side of (::) from the given alternatives based on the same logic/rule/relation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. the box reading S V / G 8.

GIVEN

• First box (D B / P W) → second box (P D / W B); third box (V 8 / S G) → ?

SOLUTION

• The four entries rotate one step clockwise: top-left→top-right, top-right→bottom-right, bottom-right→bottom-left, bottom-left→top-left.

• Check: D B/P W → after clockwise turn gives P D/W B ✓.

• Apply to V 8/S G: top-left V→top-right, 8→bottom-right, G→bottom-left, S→top-left → S V / G 8.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Just rotate the 2×2 block 90° clockwise; the letter that was bottom-left (S) lands top-left.

NOTE

• For grid analogies, track each cell's destination under the rotation instead of reading the whole box.

question: Two figures given on the left side of (::) are related with some logic/rule/relation. Select the missing figure on the right side of (::) from the given alternatives based on the same logic/rule/relation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. a black (filled) pentagon inside the box.

GIVEN

• Square (outline) → black right-angled triangle; Hexagon (outline) → ?

SOLUTION

• Rule: the second figure has one side fewer than the first AND is shaded black.

• Square (4 sides) → triangle (3 sides), filled ✓.

• Hexagon (6 sides) → pentagon (5 sides), filled = black pentagon.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Reduce the number of sides by one and shade it black: hexagon → filled pentagon.

NOTE

• In shape analogies watch two attributes at once — number of sides and shading (outline vs filled).

question: Two figures given on the left side of (::) are related with some logic/rule/relation. Select the missing figure on the right side of (::) from the given alternatives based on the same logic/rule/relation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. the box with a single dash ( – ).

GIVEN

• Box with a triangle → box with one '@'; box with a pentagon enclosing a hexagon → ?

SOLUTION

• The number of central marks equals the difference in the sides of the shapes used.

• Model pair reduces to a single symbol (one '@').

• Third figure uses a pentagon (5 sides) and a hexagon (6 sides): |6 − 5| = 1 → the answer holds one mark.

• The only option with a single symbol is the box with one dash.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Count how many small symbols the model answer carries (one); choose the option with exactly one symbol.

NOTE

• When option-figures differ only in the count of identical marks, the rule is almost always about a number derived from the left pair.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fourth letter-number cluster in the same way as the first letter-number cluster is related to the second letter-number cluster and fifth letter-number cluster is related to sixth letter-number cluster. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

GH300 : IJ207 :: ? : WX307 :: CD600 : EF507
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. UV400.

GIVEN

• GH300 : IJ207 :: ? : WX307 :: CD600 : EF507

SOLUTION

• Letters: each letter advances by +2 (G→I, H→J; C→E, D→F).

• Number: it decreases by 93 (300−93 = 207; 600−93 = 507).

• For ? : WX307, the letters of ? +2 = W,X → ? letters = U,V; and number − 93 = 307 → number = 400.

• So ? = UV400.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Reverse the map: subtract 2 from W,X to get U,V and add 93 to 307 to get 400 → UV400.

NOTE

• Handle letters and the number as two independent rules; here +2 on letters and −93 on the value.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-number cluster in the same way as the second letter-number cluster is related to the first letter-number cluster and fourth letter-number cluster is related to third letter-number cluster. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

AD40 : EJ60 :: EF60 : IL90 :: KM80 : ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. OS120.

GIVEN

• AD40 : EJ60 :: EF60 : IL90 :: KM80 : ?

SOLUTION

• First letter +4 (A→E, E→I; so K→O).

• Second letter +6 (D→J, F→L; so M→S).

• Number × 1.5 (40→60, 60→90; so 80 × 1.5 = 120).

• KM80 → OS120.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Shift letters by +4 and +6, and multiply the number by 1.5: K→O, M→S, 80→120.

NOTE

• Ratio-based number changes (×1.5) are common in MTS; verify with both model pairs before applying.

question:
Select the option that is related to the fourth number in the same way as the first number is related to the second number and fifth number is related to sixth number. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

6774 : 6823 :: ? : 5088 :: 205 : 254
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 5039.

GIVEN

• 6774 : 6823 :: ? : 5088 :: 205 : 254

SOLUTION

• Rule: second = first + 49 (6774 + 49 = 6823; 205 + 49 = 254).

• For ? : 5088, ? + 49 = 5088 → ? = 5088 − 49 = 5039.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• The constant jump is 49 (= 7²). Subtract 49 from 5088 → 5039.

NOTE

• Always test a simple constant add/subtract first; 49 = 7² is a frequently used difference.

question:
Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and sixth number is related to fifth number. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

134 : 258 :: 310 : ? :: 125 : 240
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 610.

GIVEN

• 134 : 258 :: 310 : ? :: 125 : 240

SOLUTION

• Rule: result = (number × 2) − 10.

• Check: 134×2−10 = 258 ✓; 125×2−10 = 240 ✓.

• 310×2−10 = 620 − 10 = 610.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Double the number and knock off 10: 310 → 620 → 610.

NOTE

• Try 'multiply then adjust' (×2 ± k) when the output is roughly double the input.

question: In a certain coded language 'GRASS' is coded as 'HSEPN' and 'AFORE' is coded as 'BGSOZ'. How will 'FREAK' be coded in the same code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. GSIXF.

GIVEN

• GRASS → HSEPN, AFORE → BGSOZ.

SOLUTION

• The letter-wise shifts by position are +1, +1, +4, −3, −5.

• Verify: GRASS → H,S,E,P,N ✓; AFORE → B,G,S,O,Z ✓.

• Apply to FREAK: F+1=G, R+1=S, E+4=I, A−3=X (1−3 → 24), K−5=F.

• FREAK → GSIXF.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Memorise the shift key +1,+1,+4,−3,−5 and stamp it on any 5-letter word.

NOTE

• Position-wise coding: find the +/- shift for each of the two given words; if they match, that is the rule.

question: In a certain code language, 'BEST' is coded as '64' and 'TAPE' is coded as '68'. How will 'FILED' be coded in that code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 101.

GIVEN

• BEST → 64, TAPE → 68.

SOLUTION

• Use reverse alphabet values (A=26, B=25 … Z=1, i.e. 27 − position) and add 2.

• BEST = 25+22+8+7 = 62; 62 + 2 = 64 ✓. TAPE = 7+26+11+22 = 66; 66 + 2 = 68 ✓.

• FILED: F=21, I=18, L=15, E=22, D=23 → 21+18+15+22+23 = 99; 99 + 2 = 101.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Sum of reverse-position values, then +2. FILED = 99 + 2 = 101.

NOTE

• Reverse value of a letter = 27 − its normal position (A=1…Z=26).

question:
A series is given with one term wrong. Select that wrong term from the given alternatives.

MJ108, LD181, KV252, JO324, IH396, HA468
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. LD181.

GIVEN

• MJ108, LD181, KV252, JO324, IH396, HA468

SOLUTION

• First letters: M, L, K, J, I, H → −1 each (correct throughout).

• Second letters: J, ?, V, O, H, A follow −7 each: J(10), C(3), V(22), O(15), H(8), A(1). The 2nd term should start LC, not LD.

• Numbers should rise by 72: 108, 180, 252, 324, 396, 468. The 2nd term should be 180, not 181.

• Both the letter (D vs C) and the number (181 vs 180) are wrong in LD181.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Numbers jump by 72 (108,180,252…). 181 breaks the +72 chain → LD181 is the odd term.

NOTE

• In mixed series, check the letter pattern and the number pattern separately; the wrong term usually fails one of them.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

BOT76, ?, LYD292, QDI400, VIN508
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. GTY184.

GIVEN

• BOT76, ?, LYD292, QDI400, VIN508

SOLUTION

• Every letter advances by +5 each term: B→G→L→Q→V; O→T→Y→D→I; T→Y→D→I→N.

• So the 2nd cluster = B+5, O+5, T+5 = G, T, Y.

• Numbers rise by 108: 76, 184, 292, 400, 508 → 76 + 108 = 184.

• Missing term = GTY184.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Add 5 to every letter of BOT and 108 to 76 → GTY184.

NOTE

• Confirm the common differences using the later given terms (292→400→508 = +108) before filling a gap.
